headline: Medium risk: shared network/MCP and API surfaces create injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict pathways; no direct pairwise evidence is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, while Plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and config files. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Haystack ingests untrusted outputs and forwards them into Plano. The profiles do not prove a shared channel by default, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Haystack forwards retrieved text into Plano prompts without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF Plano consumes model-visible content from Haystack as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Add a prompt delimiter and instruction/data separation rule.
Disable MCP routes that can ingest untrusted content.
Require human review before forwarding retrieved text to Plano.
Log and flag any prompt containing external instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging across the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and uses MCP/REST APIs; Plano also has broad network egress and handles logs, traces, and metrics. If they share a workspace or pass sensitive retrieval results through prompts, data can leak to external services or logs. The profiles do not show PHI or secrets, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF Haystack retrieves sensitive documents and forwards them to Plano, those contents may enter logs or traces.
IF either agent is configured to export telemetry externally, prompt or retrieval data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Turn off verbose logging for both agents.
Redact secrets before any handoff.
Restrict outbound destinations with a firewall allowlist.
Review config.yaml for telemetry and retention settings.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents into separate workspaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can use MCP and REST APIs, and Plano reads config.yaml while running out-of-process. Even without explicit filesystem write claims, both can act on shared mutable resources through APIs or configuration, so conflicting updates are plausible. The lack of documented locking or shared-write details prevents a higher severity, but uncertainty still supports medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same API-backed resource, last-write-wins conflicts can occur.
IF Plano reloads config.yaml while Haystack updates related settings, inconsistent state may result.
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces.
Freeze config.yaml during runs.
Serialize writes through one operator.
Check for concurrent edits before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system that can surface retrieved facts, and Plano is a travel-planning gateway that can consume chat completions. If Plano treats Haystack output as authoritative, retrieval errors can cascade into downstream plans or actions. The profiles do not document direct action-taking, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Plano uses Haystack output without verification, hallucinations or stale retrievals can propagate.
IF Haystack returns low-confidence snippets and Plano renders them as facts, downstream decisions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require source citations in every handoff.
Add a verification step before Plano acts on Haystack output.
Mark retrieved content as untrusted in prompts.
Sample-check outputs for factual consistency.
requires-engineering: implement confidence-aware routing.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only explicitly touch anonymous usage statistics, agentic signals, traces, metrics, logs, and config.yaml. No residency, certification, or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to logging/retention gaps rather than a clear breach. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise telemetry and handoff handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through either agent's logs or traces, retention policy mismatches become relevant.
IF deployment policy requires residency controls, external API calls may violate them.
mitigations: Confirm what data classes are allowed.
Disable or shorten log retention.
Review config.yaml for telemetry settings.
Keep regulated data out of the pair.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement.
